title: SCALING LAWS FOR MORAL MACHINE JUDGMENT IN LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS
benchmark_measurement: The paper did not measure any aspect of faith or religion. It measured the alignment of large language models' moral judgments with human preferences in the context of life-death dilemmas from the Moral Machine framework.
models_tested: Llama (including Llama 2 and Llama 3, multiple sizes)
Qwen (including Qwen1.5, Qwen2.5, Qwen3, multiple sizes)
findings: The paper's findings are unrelated to religion. The study found that as language model size increases, their moral judgments align more closely with human preferences in a predictable power-law relationship. This scaling law was robust across different model families and architectures. The paper did not analyze or report any findings related to religious beliefs, biases, or contexts.
